section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
12 Tammuz 5738*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse and the Midrashic interpretations regarding in what to rejoice.
section.t: "This is the day that the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it."1
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe of the Geulah, brings in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"
[which he said at the celebration of the first 12 Tammuz
(at the thanksgiving meal),
in the year 56882],
that it is brought in the Midrash3,
Rabbi Avin said: We do not know in what to rejoice—whether in the day or in the Holy One, blessed be He.
Shlomo came and explained4
"Let us rejoice and be glad in You"—in the Holy One, blessed be He.
"In You"—in Your fear,
"In You"—in Your Torah,
"In You"—in Your salvation.5
Rabbi Yitzchak said: "In You"—in the twenty-two letters that You have written for us in the Torah,
"Beit" (ב) is two, "Chaf" (כ) is twenty,
thus "in You" (בך).
And the maamar clarifies,
What is the meaning of "We do not know in what to rejoice—whether in the day or in the Holy One, blessed be He"?
For since "This is the day that the Lord has made"
[meaning,
that even the virtue of the day is not from itself, but rather "this is the day that the Lord has made"],
it would seemingly be understood that the joy should be in the Holy One, blessed be He,
so what is the meaning of "We do not know in what to rejoice—whether in the day or in the Holy One, blessed be He"?
And also, what are the three matters of fear, Torah, and salvation?
And also, the statement of Rabbi Yitzchak, "In You"—in the twenty-two letters, etc., must be understood,
for "in You" simply means in the Holy One, blessed be He,
so why does he interpret "in You" as the twenty-two letters?

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the elevated nature of the day on which a miracle occurred.
section.t: Now, the explanation of the virtue of the day
(to the extent that there is a possibility to think to rejoice in the day)
is6,
that the day on which a miracle occurred7
is a lofty day.
And there are two aspects to this.
For the day on which a miracle occurred is a meritorious day in its own right
(even beforehand),
therefore a miracle occurred on it,
for they bring merit through a meritorious day.8
And furthermore, through the miracle that occurred on it,
it becomes a meritorious day and an auspicious day, etc.
(even more so than it was beforehand).
Moreover, on this day itself, the primary elevation is in the specific time
(day or night)
in which the miracle occurred.
As it is brought in the Midrash9,
"When You perform miracles for us by day, we recite song before You by day
(And Devorah and Barak ben Avinoam sang on that day, etc.10),
and when You perform miracles for us by night, we recite song before You by night
(The song shall be for you as a night when a holy festival is observed11)."
